A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InFlux++ and contain 37 readable pages, including Appendices A–M. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the complete methods, equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original baseline evaluations and AnyCalib finetuning results on InFlux and InFlux++ Real in Section 5, Tables 2–3, and supplementary calibration analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original baseline evaluations, finetuning results, and supplementary calibration analyses.

M1.justification: The rendering pipeline, bounded random walk, calibration procedure, and AnyCalib architecture and objective are unchanged. The revised focal-length bound is a rendering setting, not a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain InFlux++ Synth training data and InFlux++ Real/InFlux evaluation, with unchanged scene coverage and dataset composition. The rendering-bound revision does not establish regenerated data or an added task or test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains AnyCalib, GeoCalib, UniDepthV2, WildCamera, Perspective Fields, DroidCalib, and COLMAP, alongside finetuned AnyCalib. Comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1.4 changes the reported synthetic lens focal-length range from 8–100 mm to 8–400 mm. Appendix G.2 changes the calibration screen from 5.04 × 3.06 m to 5.45 × 3.06 m, matching Section 4.2.1. These are localized revisions to reported settings; the PDFs do not establish rerun experiments.

E4.justification: The lens-breathing example, parallax comparison, and calibration-reliability diagnostics in Appendices D, I, and K are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version introduces repeated-run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The leave-one-out LUT reliability procedure in Appendix K.2 is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 and all supplementary result displays retain identical values and findings. For example, combined-set focal-length fx recall@10% remains 25.2% for AnyCalib and 31.2% after finetuning in both versions. The two numerical edits concern settings, not outcomes.

T1.justification: The thin-lens and distortion equations, mathematical definitions, and Appendix K reasoning for EPE filtering are unchanged. No assumption, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about the synthetic dataset, expanded real-world benchmark, and improved focal-length estimation through synthetic finetuning.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix L.3 retain the discussion of improved focal-length recall, generally worse principal-point/EPE recall, and the possible mismatch between AnyCalib's loss and EPE. Applicability qualifications and mechanism explanations are unchanged.

D1.justification: The rendering focal-length bound and calibration-screen width are revised technical specifications. The screen correction resolves a main-text/appendix inconsistency; other implementation details, training hyperparameters, hardware, and data/code access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 3 and all 32 references are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to InFlux, existing datasets, and calibration methods.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 6 July 2026 to v2 dated 5 September 2026. Apart from the two technical numerical substitutions, the prose, terminology, authors, and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions, and their placement are unchanged, including the appendices. Rendered comparison confirms identical body layouts; the numerical substitutions do not alter any display.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves the contradictory calibration-screen widths in Section 4.2.1 and Appendix G.2 by consistently reporting 5.45 m, providing a limited improvement in technical consistency and reproducibility. The focal-length bound is also revised, but no new validation accompanies it; the scientific evidence and conclusions remain unchanged.
